  "concordance_definition": "The paper discusses the importance of scientific validity and reproducibility in animal research for ensuring that the expected benefits of animal experiments outweigh the harms. It proposes a framework (the 3Vs: construct validity, internal validity, and external validity) to systematically assess scientific validity, similar to how the 3Rs (replace, reduce, refine) are used to minimize harm. The goal is to increase the likelihood of achieving expected benefits and avoid wasting animals for inconclusive research.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "The scope of animal experiments is often very narrow, most studies being conducted as small-scale single-laboratory studies.",
    "Due to the highly standardized conditions within laboratories, results of single-laboratory studies have often very little external validity.",
    "3R efforts to minimize animal use (reduce) may inadvertently exacerbate the situation by promoting standardization as a means to reduce within-experiment variation in view of smaller sample sizes, which can be counterproductive since standardization inevitably reduces external validity, and as a consequence reproducibility."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "50–100 million vertebrates are used in experimental procedures worldwide.",
    "for most study designs and settings, it is more likely for a research claim to be false than true",
    "less than 50% of single-laboratory studies produced an accurate estimate of the “true” effect size (reduction of infarct volume by 48%, as assessed by meta-analysis)",
    "multi-laboratory studies based on as few as three laboratories can increase reproducibility from less than 50% to over 80%"
  ]
